Three D Scans lists Location: Louvre, Material: Marble, scanned 2025 (Einstar Vega). No cast is involved; the scanned object is the ancient marble itself.

KAS1026 is therefore a cast of Ma 928. KAS1026 identifies the cast; Ma 928 identifies the original.

Restored helmet/neck portions and chipped chin mean full mesh dimensions cannot substitute for the specified two endpoints.

When a masker puts on an animal mask, he absorbs something of the animal's power. The Zamble mask of the Guro people embodies the intricate spirituality and social order of Ivory Coast societies. This ceremonial mask, used by the secretive Zamble society, represents a mythical being that is part animal and part human, a motif prevalent in Guro cosmology. The mask's elongated form, with its powerful jaws and pronounced snout, is characteristic of the noble elephant, while the graceful tusks suggest elegance and agility. The scarification patterns denote courage, beauty, and ancestral lineage. In the sacred dances, the Zamble mask becomes an animate entity, a mediator between the worlds of the living and the spirits. It is believed to possess the power to purify the village, to communicate with otherworldly beings, and to teach moral virtues.

scan_scope_caveat: The original is the polychromed terracotta model, not the marble version in Saint-Paul-Saint-Louis. The terracotta is assembled from several parts completed with stucco, seated on gypsum blocks, and was later set on a circular slab (dalle circulaire); the Louvre lists separate 'accessoire' dimensions (H 0.18 m, D 0.87 m) that probably refer to this slab, and it is not stated whether the 1.77 m height includes it. The SMK cast's gross height (173 cm) is 4 cm less than the Louvre figure, suggesting the cast omits the slab; the SMK 3D file name ('hollowback') indicates the scan is hollow at the back. Do not use raw mesh bounds without checking which base elements are present.
conflicts_or_remaining_questions: Whether the Louvre's 1.77 m includes the later circular slab base (accessory H 0.18 m) is not stated; the cast measures 173 cm gross.
The marble version (church of Saint-Paul-Saint-Louis, Paris) is a distinct object and its dimensions were not researched, since the SMK record identifies the terracotta as the original of the cast.

public_note: Dimensions of the original marble head in the Glyptothek, Munich (inv. 225); this model was scanned from a plaster cast in the SMK Royal Cast Collection.
scan_scope_caveat: The original is a head with neck stump (39 cm), once set into a herm shaft. The SMK cast (54 cm) adds a cast bust-support and round socle, so mesh bounds must be reduced to the head alone. The height was published in 1910 with the nose, horn tips and ear tips restored; if those restorations were later removed, the current head may be marginally shorter.
conflicts_or_remaining_questions: Only the 1910 museum catalogue gives a height; no modern online record for inv. 225 was found (Arachne has no Munich Zeus Ammon entry).
next_research_lead: Ask the Staatliche Antikensammlungen und Glyptothek for the current record of inv. 225, or check Fuchs 1992 no. 31 / Göttingen cast catalogue 1990 A 252 (both cited by SMK).
